theorem.statement: The answer to the differential-inverse question is affirmative.  For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), the handle \(\mathfrak I\), initialized by \(\mathfrak I_0\), defines a measurable conditional-\(X\) linear right inverse from the observed-data DQM score space into factorwise centered additive latent scores.  For every observed score \(s\), the observed conditional-expectation image of the five returned components is \(s\), and the sum of their natural factor \(L^2\)-norms is at most \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}\|s\|_{L^2(P)}\).  Consequently \(s\in\mathcal S_{\mathrm{lat}}\), and the returned class-density component is support preserving relative to every \(f_j\).
theorem.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), and let \(s\in L^2_0(P)\) be the score of an observed-data path \(\{P_t:|t|<\delta\}\) that is differentiable in quadratic mean at \(t=0\).  Define
\[
 s_X(X)=E_P(s\mid X),
 \qquad
 s_c=s-s_X.
 \tag{1}
\]
Then \(E_P(s_c\mid X)=0\).  Since conditional expectation is an orthogonal projection in \(L^2(P)\),
\[
 \|s_X\|_{L^2(P)}\leq \|s\|_{L^2(P)},
 \qquad
 \|s_c\|_{L^2(P)}\leq \|s\|_{L^2(P)}.
 \tag{2}
\]

We first justify differentiation of the conditional factorization.  Choose a measure dominating the path locally and write its densities as \(p_t\) and \(p=p_0\).  DQM means that
\[
 \sqrt{p_t}=\sqrt p+\frac{t}{2}s\sqrt p+r_t,
 \qquad
 \|r_t\|_2=o(|t|).
 \tag{3}
\]
Multiplying the sum and difference of the two square roots in (3), followed by Cauchy--Schwarz, gives
\[
 \left\|\frac{p_t-p}{t}-ps\right\|_1=o(1).
 \tag{4}
\]
Indeed, the term \(2\sqrt p r_t/t\) is \(o(1)\) in \(L^1\), and the square of \(t s\sqrt p/2+r_t\), divided by \(|t|\), is \(o(1)\) in \(L^1\).  Applying (4) first to the joint law and then to its \(X\)-marginal shows that, for every bounded measurable \(H(O)\), the conditional-moment difference quotient converges in \(L^1(P_X)\) to
\[
 \dot\mu_H(X)
 =E_P\!\left[\{H-E_P(H\mid X)\}s\mid X\right]
 =E_P(Hs_c\mid X).
 \tag{5}
\]
The equality is an equality of \(P_X\)-almost-surely defined measurable functions: it follows by integrating the signed-measure derivative in (4) against every bounded measurable function of \(X\) and using the quotient rule for the conditional numerator and the \(X\)-marginal.  Every sequence tending to zero has a subsequence along which this \(L^1(P_X)\) convergence is pointwise almost sure.  Moreover,
\[
 |\dot\mu_H(X)|
 \leq \{E_P(H^2\mid X)\}^{1/2}
       \{E_P(s_c^2\mid X)\}^{1/2}.
 \tag{6}
\]

Apply (5) to the entries of the augmented moments \((S,T_1,\ldots,T_K)\), using a pointwise-almost-sure subsequence as just described.  For \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\), the conditional factor values obey the same positivity, singular-value, and modal-label margins as a constant-\(X\) member of the model.  Lemma \(2\mathrm A\) therefore applies pointwise to the limit vector in (5).  Its uniformly bounded finite inverse maps the convergent moment difference quotients to convergent labeled-factor difference quotients.  Because the limit in (5) is unique, the resulting derivative is independent of the chosen subsequence.  We thereby recover
\[
 \dot\pi(x),\qquad \dot M_A(x),\qquad
 \dot M_Z(x),\qquad \dot\Gamma_Y(x)
 \tag{7}
\]
of the uniquely labeled factors.  The modal permutation has zero derivative because the modal gap is positive.  The inverse in Lemma \(2\mathrm A\) is a finite matrix inverse on a separated fixed-rank set.  Its Moore--Penrose formula is Borel measurable there, so the versions in (7) can be chosen measurably in \(x\).  Its uniform bound and (6) also make every coordinate in (7) finite for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\).

Let \(\Pi=\operatorname{diag}(\pi)\), and let \(p_A(y\mid x)\) be the vector with entries equal to the conditional joint densities of \((Y,A=a)\) given \(X=x\).  The identified density equation from Theorem \(1\) is
\[
 p_A(y\mid x)=M_A(x)\Pi(x)f(y\mid x).
 \tag{8}
\]
Equation (4), summed over \(Z\), supplies its conditional \(L^1(\nu)\) derivative.  Latent positivity and the surrogate-rank condition license both inverses in
\[
 \dot f
 =\Pi^{-1}M_A^{-1}
 \{\dot p_A-\dot M_A\Pi f-M_A\dot\Pi f\}.
 \tag{9}
\]
Normalization of the recovered factors gives
\[
 \sum_j\dot\pi_j=0,
 \qquad
 \sum_a\dot M_{A,aj}=0,
 \qquad
 \sum_z\dot M_{Z,zj}=0,
 \qquad
 \int_{\mathcal Y}\dot f_j,d\nu=0.
 \tag{10}
\]
Common support permits the preliminary outcome score \(u_{Y,j}=\dot f_j/f_j\), defined \(f_jd\nu\)-almost everywhere.  Also set \(u_{\pi,j}=\dot\pi_j/\pi_j\).  At a positive categorical atom set
\[
 u^A_{ja}=\frac{\dot M_{A,aj}}{M_{A,aj}},
 \qquad
 u^Z_{jz}=\frac{\dot M_{Z,zj}}{M_{Z,zj}}.
 \tag{11}
\]
At a zero atom, two-sided nonnegativity and differentiability force the corresponding derivative in (7) to be zero, and we set the ratio in (11) to zero.  Thus every preliminary factor score in (11) is centered under its own finite factor law by (10).  Differentiating the conditional product density and dividing by its positive observed density, which is licensed by common support and cell positivity, gives
\[
 s_c(y,a,z,x)
 =\sum_{j=1}^K R_{(a,z),j}(y,x)
 \{u_{\pi,j}(x)+u_{Y,j}(y,x)+u^A_{ja}(x)+u^Z_{jz}(x)\}
 \tag{12}
\]
for \(g(y\mid x)d\nu(y)dP_X(x)\)-almost every \((y,x)\) and every cell \((a,z)\).  Equation (12) is used only to prove a range identity; no square-integrability of the preliminary ratios in (11) is assumed.

Regard \(s_c(y,\cdot,x)\) as a \(K^2\)-cell vector and collect the \(2K^2\) preliminary measurement coordinates in a vector \(u(x)\), in the order \((j,a)\) and \((j,z)\) used by \(c\) and \(h\).  The terms \(u_\pi+u_Y\) in (12) form a vector in \(\operatorname{range}(R)\).  Lemma \(3\mathrm A\) gives \(N R=0\), while \(h=Nc\).  Hence
\[
 Ns_c=h^{\mathsf T}u.
 \tag{13}
\]
Define the observable conditional vector
\[
 b_s(X)=E_P\{h(Ns_c)\mid X\},
 \qquad
 u_0(X)=G(X)^+b_s(X).
 \tag{14}
\]
Equation (13) implies \(b_s=Gu\), so \(b_s\in\operatorname{range}(G)\).  Thus \(Gu_0=b_s\).  Expanding a conditional square gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_P\{(Ns_c-h^{\mathsf T}u_0)^2\mid X\}
 &=E_P\{(Ns_c)^2\mid X\}-b_s^{\mathsf T}G^+b_s,
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{15}
\]
and the left side is nonnegative.  On \(\operatorname{range}(G)\), every eigenvalue of \(G\) is at least \(\varepsilon\).  Therefore
\[
 \|u_0(X)\|_2^2
 \leq \varepsilon^{-1}u_0(X)^{\mathsf T}G(X)u_0(X)
 =\varepsilon^{-1}b_s(X)^{\mathsf T}G(X)^+b_s(X)
 \leq\varepsilon^{-1}E_P\{(Ns_c)^2\mid X\}.
 \tag{16}
\]
The same conclusion is trivial if \(G=0\).  Constant rank and the projection-Gram gap make \(G^+\) in (14) Borel measurable and uniformly bounded on its nonzero spectral subspace.

Write the two blocks of \(u_0\) as \(u^A_{0,ja}\) and \(u^Z_{0,jz}\), and recenter them by
\[
 \bar u^A_{ja}
 =u^A_{0,ja}-\sum_{a'=1}^K M_{A,a'j}u^A_{0,ja'},
 \qquad
 \bar u^Z_{jz}
 =u^Z_{0,jz}-\sum_{z'=1}^K M_{Z,z'j}u^Z_{0,jz'}.
 \tag{17}
\]
For each \(j\), subtracting a blockwise constant changes the cell contribution by a multiple of \(R_{\cdot j}\), which \(N\) annihilates.  Hence, with \(\bar u\) denoting the concatenated vector,
\[
 h^{\mathsf T}\bar u=Ns_c.
 \tag{18}
\]
Conditional Jensen applied to each mean in (17) gives, for a constant \(c_K<\infty\) depending only on fixed \(K\),
\[
 \|\bar u(X)\|_2^2\leq c_K\|u_0(X)\|_2^2.
 \tag{19}
\]
Define centered measurement-factor scores by
\[
 s_A(a,j,x)=\bar u^A_{ja}(x),
 \qquad
 s_Z(z,j,x)=\bar u^Z_{jz}(x),
 \tag{20}
\]
and let their observed contribution be
\[
 \ell(O)=E_P\{s_A(A,J,X)+s_Z(Z,J,X)\mid O\}=c(O)^{\mathsf T}\bar u(X).
 \tag{21}
\]
Their natural factor norm is bounded by \(E_P\|\bar u(X)\|_2^2\), up to a fixed factor of two.  Moreover, conditional expectation is an \(L^2\) contraction.  Lemma \(3\mathrm A\) says that \(N\) is a \(D\)-orthogonal projector; integrating first over the cells and then over \((Y,X)\) therefore yields
\[
 \|Ns_c\|_{L^2(P)}\leq\|s_c\|_{L^2(P)}.
 \tag{22}
\]
Equations (16), (19), and (22) consequently bound the factor norms in (20), and \(\|\ell\|_{L^2(P)}\), by a constant depending only on \(K\) and \(\varepsilon\), times \(\|s_c\|_{L^2(P)}\).

Set
\[
 s_0=s_c-\ell.
 \tag{23}
\]
Equations (18), (21), and (23) give \(Ns_0=0\).  By Lemma \(3\mathrm A\), \(\ker(N)=\operatorname{range}(R)\).  The posterior-Gram gap makes \(R^{\mathsf T}DR\) invertible, so the unique coefficient vector satisfying \(s_0=R\tau\) is
\[
 \tau(y,x)=\{R(y,x)^{\mathsf T}D(y,x)R(y,x)\}^{-1}
 R(y,x)^{\mathsf T}D(y,x)s_0(y,\cdot,x).
 \tag{24}
\]
For each \((y,x)\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_{j=1}^K w_j(y,x)\tau_j(y,x)^2
 &\leq \|\tau(y,x)\|_2^2\\
 &\leq\varepsilon^{-1}\tau(y,x)^{\mathsf T}R(y,x)^{\mathsf T}D(y,x)R(y,x)\tau(y,x)\\
 &=\varepsilon^{-1}s_0(y,\cdot,x)^{\mathsf T}D(y,x)s_0(y,\cdot,x).
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{25}
\]
Multiplication by \(g(y\mid x)\), integration with respect to \(\nu\), and the identity \(gw_j=\pi_jf_j\) transform (25) into
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^K\pi_j(X)\int_{\mathcal Y}f_j(y\mid X)\tau_j(y,X)^2d\nu(y)
 \leq\varepsilon^{-1}E_P(s_0^2\mid X).
 \tag{26}
\]

Now define
\[
 s_{\pi,j}(x)=\int_{\mathcal Y}f_j(y\mid x)\tau_j(y,x)d\nu(y),
 \qquad
 s_{Y,j}(y,x)=\tau_j(y,x)-s_{\pi,j}(x).
 \tag{27}
\]
The second score in (27) is centered under \(f_j(\cdot\mid x)d\nu\).  The scores in (20) are centered by construction, so \(E_P(\ell\mid X)=0\).  Equations (1) and (23) then give \(E_P(s_0\mid X)=0\).  On the other hand, \(s_0=R\tau\), \(\sum_{a,z}d_{az}R_{(a,z),j}=w_j\), and \(gw_j=\pi_jf_j\) imply
\[
 0=E_P(s_0\mid X)=\sum_{j=1}^K\pi_j(X)s_{\pi,j}(X).
 \tag{28}
\]
Thus \(s_\pi\) is centered under the conditional law of \(J\) given \(X\).  Conditional Jensen and (26) give
\[
 \|s_\pi\|_{\mathrm{factor}}^2
 \leq\|\tau\|_{\mathrm{factor}}^2,
 \qquad
 \|s_Y\|_{\mathrm{factor}}^2
 \leq\|\tau\|_{\mathrm{factor}}^2
 \leq\varepsilon^{-1}\|s_0\|_{L^2(P)}^2.
 \tag{29}
\]

It remains to verify the right-inverse identity.  Conditioning the sum of the five constructed factor scores on \(O\), and using (21), (24), and (27), yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &E_P\{s_X(X)+s_\pi(J,X)+s_Y(Y,J,X)
       +s_A(A,J,X)+s_Z(Z,J,X)\mid O\}\\
 &\qquad=s_X+R\tau+\ell
 =s_X+s_0+\ell
 =s.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{30}
\]
All operations in (1), (14), (17), (21), (24), and (27) are linear in \(s\).  Their matrices and conditional expectations have measurable versions.  The fixed-rank Moore--Penrose map in (14) and the uniformly positive-definite inverse in (24) are Borel measurable.  Thus the construction is a measurable conditional-\(X\) linear right inverse.

Finally, (2), (16), (19), (22), (23), (26), and (29), together with the contraction bound for (21), give
\[
 \|s_X\|_{\mathrm{factor}}+\|s_\pi\|_{\mathrm{factor}}
 +\|s_Y\|_{\mathrm{factor}}+\|s_A\|_{\mathrm{factor}}
 +\|s_Z\|_{\mathrm{factor}}
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\|s\|_{L^2(P)}.
 \tag{31}
\]
Every division and inversion used above is licensed respectively by latent positivity, common support, cell positivity, the surrogate-rank condition, the posterior-Gram gap, and the projection-Gram rank and gap assumptions.

For completeness, the outcome score in (27) changes no support: it is defined \(f_jd\nu\)-almost everywhere and introduces no component outside \(\{f_j>0\}\).  It is also the DQM score of strictly positive, same-support conditional densities.  To see this directly, let \(a_t=|t|^{-1/2}\), let \(v_{t,j}\) be \(s_{Y,j}\) truncated to \([-a_t,a_t]\) and then recentered under \(f_j(\cdot\mid x)d\nu\), and put
\[
 f_{j,t}(y\mid x)
 =f_j(y\mid x)
 \frac{\exp\{t v_{t,j}(y,x)\}}
 {\int_{\mathcal Y}\exp\{t v_{t,j}(u,x)\}f_j(u\mid x)d\nu(u)}.
 \tag{32}
\]
Then \(v_{t,j}\to s_{Y,j}\) in the factor \(L^2\) norm, while \(\|tv_{t,j}\|_\infty=O(|t|^{1/2})\).  A second-order expansion of the two exponentials in the square root of (32), with remainder bounded uniformly because \(tv_{t,j}\to0\) uniformly, gives
\[
 \left\|
 \frac{\sqrt{f_{j,t}}-\sqrt{f_j}}{t}
 -\frac12s_{Y,j}\sqrt{f_j}
 \right\|_2\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{33}
\]
Thus (32) is DQM with score \(s_{Y,j}\); its density ratio is strictly positive, so its support equals that of \(f_j\) for every sufficiently small nonzero \(t\).  This proves the asserted support-preserving recovery and completes the construction of \(\mathfrak I\).

proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(\|V\|_2=\{E_P\|V\|^2\}^{1/2}\) for a random vector or matrix, using the Euclidean, Frobenius, or operator norm appropriate to its type.  All constants below may change from line to line but depend only on the quantities allowed in \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}\).

First consider the pointwise cell projector.  Put
\[
 H=B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B,
 \qquad
 \widehat H=\widehat B^{\mathsf T}\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B.
 \tag{41}
\]
Observed-cell positivity, namely \(d_{az}(Y,X)\geq\varepsilon\), and the fitted half-margin in the coherent-fit definition imply
\[
 \|D^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\varepsilon^{-1},
 \qquad
 \|\widehat D^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq2\varepsilon^{-1}.
 \tag{42}
\]
Moreover, if \(v\in\mathbb R^K\), matricizing \(Bv\) and using the Khatri--Rao definition of \(B\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{mat}(Bv)=M_A\operatorname{diag}(v)M_Z^{\mathsf T}.
\]
The surrogate- and proxy-rank assumptions therefore give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|Bv\|_2
 &=\|M_A\operatorname{diag}(v)M_Z^{\mathsf T}\|_{\mathrm F}\\
 &\geq \sigma_{\min}(M_A)\sigma_{\min}(M_Z)
       \|\operatorname{diag}(v)\|_{\mathrm F}
 \geq\varepsilon^2\|v\|_2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{43}
\]
The same argument, with the fitted half-margins, yields
\(\|\widehat Bv\|_2\geq(\varepsilon^2/4)\|v\|_2\).  Because every diagonal entry of \(D\) and \(\widehat D\) is a probability and hence at most one,
\[
 v^{\mathsf T}Hv=\|D^{-1/2}Bv\|_2^2\geq\|Bv\|_2^2,
 \qquad
 v^{\mathsf T}\widehat Hv\geq\|\widehat Bv\|_2^2.
\]
Consequently \(H\) and \(\widehat H\) are invertible and
\[
 \|H^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\varepsilon^{-4},
 \qquad
 \|\widehat H^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq16\varepsilon^{-4}.
 \tag{44}
\]
Thus the Moore--Penrose inverses in the two cell-projector formulas are ordinary inverses.

The exact resolvent identities
\[
 \widehat D^{-1}-D^{-1}
 =\widehat D^{-1}(D-\widehat D)D^{-1},
 \qquad
 \widehat H^{-1}-H^{-1}
 =\widehat H^{-1}(H-\widehat H)H^{-1}
 \tag{45}
\]
and a four-factor telescoping of \(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B\) imply, using the uniform bounds in (42)--(44),
\[
 \|\widehat H-H\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}
 \bigl(\|\widehat B-B\|_{\mathrm{op}}
       +\|\widehat D-D\|_{\mathrm{op}}\bigr).
 \tag{46}
\]
Apply (45)--(46) to
\[
 N_B=I_{K^2}-D^{-1}BH^{-1}B^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 \widehat N=I_{K^2}-\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B
                    \widehat H^{-1}\widehat B^{\mathsf T}.
\]
A second product telescoping gives pointwise
\[
 \|\widehat N-N_B\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}
 \bigl(\|\widehat D-D\|_{\mathrm{op}}
       +\|\widehat B-B\|_{\mathrm{op}}\bigr).
 \tag{47}
\]
Taking the declared conditional \(L^2(P)\) norm proves
\[
 \{E_P\|\widehat N-N_B\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\}^{1/2}
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_D+r_B).
 \tag{48}
\]

We next control the conditional Gram step.  The projection-Gram gap says that every nonzero eigenvalue of \(G(X)\) is at least \(\varepsilon\), and the coherent fit uses the observable threshold \(\tau_G=\varepsilon/2\).  The already established data-driven Gram-threshold lemma therefore gives
\[
 \|\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}-G^+\|_{L^2(P_X;\mathrm{op})}
 \leq26\varepsilon^{-2}r_G,
 \qquad
 \|\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq2\varepsilon^{-1}.
 \tag{49}
\]
It also gives, on the event \(r_{G,\infty}<\varepsilon/4\), equality of the threshold-selected rank and \(\operatorname{rank}(G(X))\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\).  Since \(r_{G,\infty}=o_P(1)\), this event has probability tending to one.  Hence rank recovery is a conclusion from the fitted spectrum and not an oracle input.

All remaining plug-in maps are uniformly bounded on the true and fitted regular strata.  Indeed, bounded outcome support gives \(|m_j|\vee|\widehat m_j|\leq L\); latent positivity and its fitted half-margin bound the inverse propensities; the true and fitted measurement singular-value margins bound the inverse bridges; \(R\) and \(\widehat R\) are posterior matrices from their respective coherent product laws; and (42), (44), and (49) bound the projector and generalized-inverse factors.  Conditional expectation is an \(L^2\)-contraction.  It follows by applying (45), the analogous identity
\[
 \widehat M^{-1}-M^{-1}
 =\widehat M^{-1}(M-\widehat M)M^{-1},
 \tag{50}
\]
and product telescoping successively to \(R\), \(N\), \(c\), \(h\), \(G\), and \(b_{(\cdot)}\) that one differentiated factor is measured by its declared coordinate of \(r_\eta\), while all undifferentiated factors are bounded by \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}\).  In particular,
\[
 \|\widehat U-U\|_2
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_m+r_\pi+r_A+r_Z)
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma.
 \tag{51}
\]
Here the bridge part follows directly from (50): for example,
\(\widehat M_A^{-1}M_A-I=widehat M_A^{-1}(M_A-\widehat M_A)\), and similarly for \(M_Z\).  Since \(R_\Sigma\) is the sum of nonnegative declared errors and contains \(r_R,r_N,r_h,r_G,r_b\), it also gives directly
\[
 r_R+r_N+r_h+r_G+r_b\leq R_\Sigma,
 \tag{52}
\]
which is the asserted \(O_P(R_\Sigma)\) bound.

For completeness, let \(\widehat b_{\widehat U}\) denote the fitted-law right-hand side formed coherently from \(\widehat U\).  Add and subtract one factor at a time in the Gram correction:
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\widehat h^{\mathsf T}\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}
       \widehat b_{\widehat U}-h^{\mathsf T}G^+b_U\\
 &\quad=(\widehat h-h)^{\mathsf T}\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}
              \widehat b_{\widehat U}
 +h^{\mathsf T}(\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}-G^+)
              \widehat b_{\widehat U}
 +h^{\mathsf T}G^+(\widehat b_{\widehat U}-b_U).
\end{aligned}
\tag{53}
\]
The uniform bounds just established, conditional Cauchy--Schwarz, (49), and the definitions of \(r_h,r_G,r_b\) yield
\[
 \|\widehat h^{\mathsf T}\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}
       \widehat b_{\widehat U}-h^{\mathsf T}G^+b_U\|_2
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_h+r_G+r_b)
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma.
 \tag{54}
\]
Likewise, (47), (51), and the boundedness of \(N_B,\widehat N,U,\widehat U\) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|\widehat N\widehat U-N_BU\|_2
 &\leq\|(\widehat N-N_B)\widehat U\|_2
       +\|N_B(\widehat U-U)\|_2\\
 &\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma.
\end{aligned}
\tag{55}
\]
Subtracting (54) from (55) according to the definitions of \(\widehat Q\) and \(Q\), and then using the triangle inequality, proves
\[
 \|\widehat Q\widehat U-QU\|_{L^2(P)}
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma.
 \tag{56}
\]
Finally,
\[
 (\widehat U-\widehat Q\widehat U)-(U-QU)
 =(\widehat U-U)-(\widehat Q\widehat U-QU),
\]
so (51), (56), and the triangle inequality establish the same linear \(L^2(P)\) bound for the full estimated efficient score.

Work coordinatewise and put \(k=QU\) and \(\widehat k=\widehat Q\widehat U\).  The already established support-leakage conditional-zero lemma applies because both objects are formed from the same coherent fitted product law and the same data-driven spectral inverse.  If \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\), its event \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{supp},n}\) has probability tending to one, and on that event
\[
 \|E_P\widehat k\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\left[
 (r_A+r_Z)\|\widehat k-k\|_{L^2(P)}+r_Ar_Z
 +\ell_{A,n}+\ell_{Z,n}\right].
 \tag{57}
\]
The score-stability lemma just proved gives
\(\|\widehat k-k\|_{L^2(P)}\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma\).  Hence
\[
 \|E_P\widehat k\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}
 \{(r_A+r_Z)R_\Sigma+r_Ar_Z
   +\ell_{A,n}+\ell_{Z,n}\}.
 \tag{58}
\]

It remains to evaluate the raw bridge mean.  For \(j,\ell\in\mathcal J\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \delta^A_{j\ell}(X)
 &=E_P\{\widehat a_j(A,X)\mid J=\ell,X\}
   -\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\},\\
 \delta^Z_{j\ell}(X)
 &=E_P\{\widehat z_j(Z,X)\mid J=\ell,X\}
   -\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{59}
\]
By the bridge definitions and the true conditional laws of \(A\) and \(Z\), these matrices satisfy the exact identities
\[
 \delta^A=\widehat M_A^{-1}M_A-I_K
 =\widehat M_A^{-1}(M_A-\widehat M_A),
 \qquad
 \delta^Z=\widehat M_Z^{-1}M_Z-I_K
 =\widehat M_Z^{-1}(M_Z-\widehat M_Z).
 \tag{60}
\]
The fitted singular-value half-margins and the definition of \(r_A,r_Z\) therefore imply
\[
 \|\delta^A\|_{L^2(P_X)}\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A,
 \qquad
 \|\delta^Z\|_{L^2(P_X)}\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_Z,
 \tag{61}
\]
and both matrices are uniformly bounded.

Conditional three-view independence implies that, given \((J=\ell,X)\), the three factors \(Y\), \(A\), and \(Z\) separate.  Consistently with the definition of \(m_\ell\),
\(E_P(Y-\widehat m_j\mid J=\ell,X)=m_\ell-\widehat m_j\).  Expanding the definition of \(\widehat U_j\), conditioning first on \((J,X)\), and then summing over \(J\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P(\widehat U_j\mid X)-m_j
={}&(\widehat m_j-m_j)
 \left[1-\frac{\pi_j}{\widehat\pi_j}
 (1+\delta^A_{jj})(1+\delta^Z_{jj})\right]\\
&+\widehat\pi_j^{-1}\sum_{\ell\ne j}\pi_\ell
 \delta^A_{j\ell}\delta^Z_{j\ell}
 (m_\ell-\widehat m_j).
\end{aligned}
\tag{62}
\]
This identity is exact: for \(\ell=j\) both conditional bridge means are \(1+\delta_{jj}\), whereas for \(\ell\ne j\) both indicator terms vanish and only the product of the two errors remains.

The true latent-positivity assumption and the fitted half-margin give \(\pi_j^{-1}\leq\varepsilon^{-1}\) and \(\widehat\pi_j^{-1}\leq2\varepsilon^{-1}\).  Also \(|m_\ell|\vee|\widehat m_j|\leq L\) because both regressions arise from laws supported on the declared bounded outcome support.  From
\[
 \left|1-\frac{\pi_j}{\widehat\pi_j}
ight|
 \leq2\varepsilon^{-1}|\widehat\pi_j-\pi_j|
\]
and the uniform bounds on \(\delta^A,\delta^Z\), the absolute value of the first line of (62), integrated over \(X\), is at most
\[
 C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_m(r_\pi+r_A+r_Z),
\]
by Cauchy--Schwarz.  The second line is at most \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_Ar_Z\), again by Cauchy--Schwarz applied to (61), using that \(K\) is fixed.  Since \(E_Pm_j(X)=\psi_j\), summing the finitely many coordinates yields
\[
 \|E_P\widehat U-\psi\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}
 \{r_m(r_\pi+r_A+r_Z)+r_Ar_Z\}.
 \tag{63}
\]
The mean of the estimated efficient score obeys
\[
 E_P(\widehat U-\widehat Q\widehat U)-\psi
 =(E_P\widehat U-\psi)-E_P\widehat k.
\]
Combining (58), (63), and the definition of \(\Delta_n\) proves, on \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{supp},n}\),
\[
 \|E_P(\widehat U-\widehat Q\widehat U)-\psi\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\Delta_n.
 \tag{64}
\]
The probability of that event tends to one, as required.

We finally verify the two derivative assertions without using a rate bound as a substitute for the cancellation.  Let \(t\mapsto\eta_t\) be a support-preserving two-sided regular perturbation with \(\eta_0=\eta\), and evaluate its score mean under \(P=P_{\eta_0}\).  If only \(M_A\) varies, then \(m_t=m\), \(\pi_t=\pi\), and \(\delta^Z_t=0\).  Equation (62) consequently gives
\[
 E_PU(\eta_t)-\psi=0
 \quad\text{for all sufficiently small }t.
 \tag{65}
\]
Support preservation makes the off-support leakage exactly zero.  The conditional-zero inequality with \(r_Z=0\), together with the locally Lipschitz plug-in bounds (45)--(56), gives
\[
 \|E_P Q(\eta_t)U(\eta_t)\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A(t)
 \|Q(\eta_t)U(\eta_t)-QU\|_2
 =O(t^2),
 \tag{66}
\]
because differentiability of the path gives \(r_A(t)=O(|t|)\), and the separated inverse and Gram-gap bounds give score displacement \(O(|t|)\).  Equations (65)--(66) show that the derivative at zero of the mean bias is zero.

If only \(f\) varies coherently, then \(M_A,M_Z,\pi\), and hence \(B\), do not vary, so \(\delta^A_t=\delta^Z_t=0\).  Equation (62) again gives the exact equality \(E_PU(\eta_t)=\psi\), even though \(m_t\) may vary.  Furthermore, the projector algebra gives \(B^{\mathsf T}N_t=0\).  Since every column of \(h_t=N_tc_t\) also lies in \(\ker(B^{\mathsf T})\), the definition of \(Q_t\) implies, cellwise,
\[
 B^{\mathsf T}\{Q_tU(\eta_t)\}=0.
 \tag{67}
\]
Conditional three-view independence identifies the \(j\)-th coordinate of the left side with
\[
 E_P\{Q_tU(\eta_t)\mid Y,J=j,X\}
 =\sum_{a,z}B_{(a,z),j}
   \{Q_tU(\eta_t)\}_{a,z}(Y,X)=0.
\]
Iterated expectation therefore gives \(E_PQ_tU(\eta_t)=0\) exactly.  Together with the raw equality, this shows that the mean bias is identically zero along the coherent \(f\)-only perturbation, and in particular its pathwise derivative at zero vanishes.
